statements.verbatim_passage: To reduce to the risk of wildfire ignition, power system operators execute "Public Safety Power Shutoff" (PSPS) events that temporarily deenergize power lines that run through areas with high ignition risk.
statements.passage_as_proposed: To reduce to the risk of wildfire ignition, power system operators execute "Public Safety Power Shutoff" (PSPS) events that temporarily deenergize power lines that run through areas with high ignition risk. Since de‑energized lines cannot ignite wildfires, PSPS strategies are effective at immediately reducing the ignition risks posed by an electric power system. However, the partially de‑energized system may be incapable of supplying all load demands, leading to power outages that have negative economic, health, and safety impacts.

time.quote: ten‑day period from June 13, 2021 to June 22, 2021

proposal.statement: Higher wildfire ignition risk, as measured by the Wind‑enhanced Fire Potential Index, leads utilities to de‑energize transmission lines, which increases load shedding on the power system.

statements.verbatim_passage: In this work, we use forecasts of the Wind-enhanced Fire Potential Index (WFPI) produced by the United States Geological Survey as a surrogate for more complex riskassignment methods [28].
statements.passage_as_proposed: In this work, we use forecasts of the Wind‑enhanced Fire Potential Index (WFPI) produced by the United States Geological Survey as a surrogate for more complex risk‑assignment methods. WFPI values, which range from 0 to 150, are based on conditions such as wind speed, rain, temperature, etc. Large fires are associated with the highest WFPI values. To assign a wildfire ignition risk, r, to each line ∈ L, we integrate the WFPI index along the line's path.

proposal.statement: Using forecasts of the Wind‑enhanced Fire Potential Index as a surrogate fire‑weather index allows the assignment of line‑specific wildfire risk values for optimization of de‑energization decisions.
